title: Israel Crosses the Jordan under Joshua
summary: On the 10th day of the 1st month Israel crosses the Jordan into Canaan (Josh 4:19), after the 40 years in the wilderness.
description: Judges-period record added from James B. Jordan's chronology (secondary display) with Ussher, Jones and, where available, CFAH-1 Table 1 dates for sorting. Jordan treats the judgeships as partly overlapping regional sequences (North / Centre / South) fitted to the 480 years of 1 Kgs 6:1 and the 300 years of Judg 11:26.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones baseline): 1450 BC (no CFAH anchor point for this event). Jordan (secondary display) never sets the sort.

chronologies.date: 1450 BC (Crossing the Jordan; "differs by 1 year from Jones")
chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
chronologies.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point.

chronologies.date: "JOSHUA CROSSED JORDAN 1st MONTH 10th DAY = THURSDAY, APRIL 2, BC 1451"
chronologies.citation: Jones, Chart No. 4 "Judges to the First 3 Kings" (© 1993 Floyd Jones; chart text revised "As of 2007"), box "Chronology for the Conquering of Heshbon" (Josh 3:15, 4:19)
chronologies.note: Jones, 15th ed. (2002), ch. V p. 90: "the crossing of Jordan took place in BC 1451 (AM 2553)".

chronologies.date: 2553c AM, 1451 BC; 10th day of the 1st month (Friday, April 30)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §307 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

chronologies.date: 1st Month 2554, "Day 10: Israel crosses Jordan (Joshua 4:19); Passover lambs set aside."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, A Chronological and Calendrical Commentary on the Pentateuch (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 3, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 19 "The Years 2553 and 2554", p. 54 (day list)
chronologies.note: 2001. Same year in From Creation to Solomon (2001), p. 51 summary: "2554 - Beginning of Conquest of the land." Jordan's year here turns at the 7th month, so his 1st month of 2554 follows Moses' death on 11/1/2554. One year later than Ussher/Jones AM 2553.

chronologies.date: "2553 - Beginning of Conquest of the land."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
chronologies.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory). Same essay: "Since the invasion of the land came in A.M. 2553 ...".

chronologies.date: Mar. – Apr. 2554 A.M. was the “1st month, 10th day” when Joshua crossed the Jordan River (Josh. 4:19).
chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 6, chart "Year of the World: From Joseph’s death to the Judges"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2554.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 6 "The Special People of God", PDF p. 184 (printed p. 183)
chronologies.note: Heading "Moving into the Promised Land"; Timeline Review (p. 212): "Joshua Takes Promised Land 1406 bc". Differs from the sort year (1450 BC, cfah-table1) by 44 years.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "1450 BC" (PDF p. 308): 44 years earlier.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 13 "The Special People of God–Taking the Promised Land", PDF p. 308 (printed p. 294)
